title: Strict coordinate models for punctual dg Hom and finite principal localization
statement:
Let $S$ be a commutative ring and let $C$ be a left dg $S$-algebra on the punctual site, using [def-sfb-sheaf-dg-module-localization] over the punctual ring sheaf $\underline S$ with its evaluation at the point from [def-trf-singleton-site-operations]; this evaluation is an exact tensor-compatible equivalence by [lem-weil-pbc-singleton-site-module-comparison]. All complexes are integer cochain complexes, without boundedness. A strict dg Hom model is a bifunctor on pairs of left dg modules, contravariant in the first variable, to $S$-complexes, with injective $S$-linear degree-$q$ coordinates whose image is exactly the graded $C$-linear maps $h(cx)=(-1)^{q|c|}ch(x)$, differential $d_Nh-(-1)^qhd_P$, and maps given by pre- and postcomposition. A module $P$ is homotopically projective when its Hom complex into every acyclic module is acyclic.
For $f\in S$, a principal localization model consists of an $S$-dg algebra $C_f$ and a dg algebra map $C\to C_f$ whose degreewise maps are module localizations at $\{1,f,f^2,\ldots\}$. Ordinary extension is the balanced extension of [def-sfb-sheaf-dg-module-localization], restriction retains the underlying complex, and their adjunction has the specified action counit $b\otimes n\mapsto bn$, fixing its unit to $x\mapsto1\otimes x$; that unit is degreewise the same module localization. Both functors preserve quasi-isomorphisms. Their derived functors on the specified localizations have comparison isomorphisms with ordinary extension and restriction, and a derived adjunction whose unit is induced from the ordinary unit. Coefficient derived categories use [def-weil-abstract-derived-category].
Given $r\in\mathbf N$ and $f:\{1,\ldots,r\}\to S$, index intersections by nonempty subsets $J$ and put $f_J=\prod_{j\in J}f_j$. A local Hom diagram consists of such localization and Hom models for every $f_J$, with further-localization maps commuting with the localization units. Hom restriction and transition maps are natural chain maps uniquely fixed on fractions by $h(x/1)=h(x)/1$ and by further localization, respectively.
A finite alternating Cech model for this diagram is a functorial double complex $B$ with specified $S$-linear coordinate isomorphisms $B^{p,q}\cong\prod_{|J|=p+1}\operatorname{Hom}_{C_{f_J}}^q(P_{f_J},N_{f_J})$. Its vertical differential is the Hom differential; its horizontal differential is the alternating sum of the localization transitions, ordered by increasing indices, with sign $(-1)^k$ when the $k$-th index is deleted. Coordinates intertwine module maps. Its total is the direct-sum total with differential $\delta+(-1)^pd_{\rm Hom}$. The augmentation is the natural chain map given by all singleton Hom restrictions in column zero and zero in every higher column. These are specifications of data; their existence and the augmentation being a quasi-isomorphism are not part of this definition.
